questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution aim to create a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Welfare State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to establish India as a welfare state.
 
• These principles are enshrined in **Part IV **of the Constitution of India and are intended to guide the state in formulating policies and laws.
 
• They emphasize social and economic democracy, aiming to reduce inequalities and ensure a decent standard of living for all citizens.
 
• Key areas include providing adequate means of livelihood, **equal pay for equal work**, **protection of children and youth**, and securing a social order based on **justice **and **equality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on **26th November 1949 **and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and the objective is to create a social framework that supports the well-being of all citizens.
 
• Though non-justiciable, the principles act as a moral compass for the state in creating laws and policies aimed at social welfare and public good.
 
• The implementation of these principles is seen as crucial for achieving the goals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution.

questions.question: The Simon Commission, appointed in 1927, was criticized in India because:

options.text: It did not include any Indian members
It recommended the withdrawal of British rule from India
It recommended constitutional reforms for India
It proposed to divide India into two separate countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It did not include any Indian members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of introducing the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms in 1919, the British Government declared that a commission would be sent to India after ten years.
 
• To examine the effects and operations of the constitutional reforms and to suggest more reforms for India.
 
• 1919 Montegue-Chelmsford Act could not achieve much and the Simon Commission was appointed.
 
• The Simon Report was met with disappointment and condemnation throughout India.
 
• The Simon Commission was dispatched to India in 1928 to review the Government of India Act 1919.
 
• The Commission, appointed by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin, did not include any Indian delegates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian National Congress and a faction of the Muslim League, led by Mohammed Ali Jinnah, decided to boycott the Commission.
 
• Upon arrival in Bombay on 3 February 1928, the Commission was met by protests.
 
• In London, the London Branch of the Indian National Congress planned a demonstration upon the return of the Commission.
 
• Indian National Congress mistrusted the findings of the Commission and the Congress boycotted the Report.
 
• The commission arrived in** British India **in **1928 **to study constitutional reform in Britain's largest and most important possession.
 
• One of its members was the future leader of the **Labor Party** Clement Attlee, who became committed to self-government for India.
 
• It was necessary to thwart the increasing prominence of the **Swaraj Party.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

__
 
• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is a domestic cricket competition in India, organized by the BCCI, featuring List A matches.
 
• The **Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy** is another domestic cricket tournament organized by the BCCI, focusing on T20 matches.
 
• Both tournaments are part of India's domestic cricket structure and serve as platforms for selecting players for international matches.
 
• While the Vijay Hazare Trophy is played in a 50-over format, the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy is a shorter format with **20 **overs per side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijay Hazare Trophy:** Named after legendary cricketer Vijay Hazare, this tournament is a 50-over competition often considered the domestic equivalent of One Day Internationals (ODIs).
 
• **Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy:** Named after the Indian cricketer Syed Mushtaq Ali, this tournament is focused on T20 cricket and has contributed significantly to the development of India's T20 talent pool.
 
• BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) organizes these tournaments to provide a structured pathway for players to showcase their skills at a professional level.
 
• Performances in these tournaments often influence selection for **IPL teams** and the **Indian national cricket team**.

questions.question: Population Census in India is conducted within a span of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10** **Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The census of India is conducted at an interval of 10 years.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872.
 
• As of 2021, India's decennial census has been carried out 16 times. 
 
• The first comprehensive census was done in 1881, but it had been conducted every ten years since Viceroy Lord Mayo took office in 1872.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Since 1949, it has been managed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, through the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India. 
 
• The 1948 Census of India Act, which predates the Indian Constitution, has been used to conduct all censuses since 1951.
 
• The Union Government is not required by the 1948 Census of India Act to carry out the Census on a specific day or to make the results available within a specified timeframe.
 
• The census provides information on the size, distribution, and socio-economic characteristics of the population.
 
• The latest census in India was conducted in 2011, and the next one is scheduled for 2021.

questions.question: Who was selected as the recipient of the 41st Lokmanya Tilak Award, on 1st August 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

__
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred with the **41st Lokmanya Tilak National Award** on August 1, 2023, in **Pune**, Maharashtra.
 
• This award is presented annually by the Tilak Smarak Mandir Trust, instituted in **1983**.
 
• PM Modi dedicated the award to India's 140 crore citizens and announced his decision to donate the cash prize to the Namami Gange Project.
 
• The award commemorates the death anniversary of Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a key figure in India's freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Previous Recipients:** The award has been conferred upon notable leaders such as **Indira Gandhi**, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, **Pranab Mukherjee**, and **Dr. Shankar Dayal Sharma**.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** A prominent leader of India's independence movement, he is remembered as "**Lokmanya**" for his advocacy of **Swaraj** (self-rule).
 
• **Namami Gange Project:** A flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at cleaning and rejuvenating the **Ganga River**.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023 introduced by ______ ministry in 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023**, was introduced by the Ministry of Home Affairs in 2023.
 
• This bill aims to replace the colonial-era **Code of Criminal Procedure** (**CrPC**), 1973, with updated provisions to enhance the criminal justice system in India.
 
• The bill introduces mandatory forensic investigations for offenses punishable with seven years of imprisonment or more, along with provisions for electronic trials and proceedings.
 
• It seeks to **digitize **the entire process from **FIR to judgment**, ensuring **transparency** and **efficiency **in criminal proceedings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):** The MHA oversees internal security, border management, and the administration of Union Territories in India.
 
• **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973:** The CrPC is the primary legislation that outlines the procedures for administering criminal law in India.
 
• **Forensic Investigation:** Involves applying scientific methods to investigate crimes and gather evidence.
 
• **Electronic Trials:** Use of digital platforms and tools for conducting legal proceedings to enhance accessibility and efficiency.
 
• The introduction of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023, demonstrates the government's commitment to modernizing the **criminal justice system** and addressing contemporary needs with technological advancements.

• **Incentive to Remission:** Transitioning to remission-based schemes like RoDTEP to refund duties and taxes to exporters.
 
• **Export Promotion through Collaboration:** Enhancing cooperation among exporters, states, districts, and Indian missions to boost exports.
 
• **Ease of Doing Business and E-Initiatives:** Simplifying trade procedures, reducing costs, and leveraging technology through e-initiatives.
 
• **Developing Emerging Sectors:** Promoting new-age industries like **e-commerce**, **green energy**, and **electronics** to integrate India into global value chains and drive future growth.
 
 
 
• The policy does not emphasize Restriction on Imports as a pillar, focusing instead on **export promotion** and **trade facilitation**.
 
• The policy aims to achieve a $2 trillion export target by 2030, reflecting India's commitment to becoming a global trade leader.

questions.question: As per which article of the Indian Constitution, the Lok Sabha is the lower House of the parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**79**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Lok Sabha plays a critical role in the legislative process, passing laws, and controlling the executive through motions like no-confidence motions.
 
• Article 79 of the Indian Constitution specifies the composition of the Parliament of India, which includes the Lok Sabha, or House of the People, as the lower house.
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Parliament of India and consists of representatives directly elected by the people.
 
• Article 80: Defines the composition of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), the upper house
